spots.name: St. Martin's Cathedral, Utrecht
spots.summary: St. Martin's Cathedral, Utrecht, or Dom Church, is a Gothic church dedicated to Saint Martin of Tours, which was the cathedral of the Diocese of Utrecht during the Middle Ages. It is the country's only pre-Reformation cathedral, but has been a Protestant church since 1580.

spots.name: Dom Tower of Utrecht
spots.summary: The Dom Tower of Utrecht is the tallest church tower in the Netherlands, at 112.32 metres (368.5 feet) in height. It is considered the symbol of Utrecht. The tower was part of St. Martin's Cathedral, also known as the Dom Church, and was built between 1321 and 1382, to a design by John of Hainaut.

spots.name: Rietveld Schröder House

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Rietveld Schröder House in Utrecht was built in 1924 by Dutch architect Gerrit Rietveld for Mrs. Truus Schröder-Schräder and her three children.

spots.name: St Catherine's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Catherine's Cathedral, often referred to as Catharijnekerk, is a Catholic church dedicated to Saint Catherine of Alexandria situated in Utrecht in the Netherlands.

spots.name: Buurkerk

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Buurkerk is a former church building in Utrecht (city), Netherlands on the Buurkerkhof. The building is the location of the Museum Speelklok, and the entrance is on the Steenweg. It is one of the medieval parish churches of Utrecht, along with the Jacobikerk, the Nicolaïkerk and the Geertekerk.

spots.name: St. Peter's Church, Utrecht

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Peter's Church is a Reformed and former Roman Catholic church in the city of Utrecht in the Netherlands, dedicated to Peter the Apostle. It is one of the city's oldest churches. Its construction began in 1039 and it was inaugurated on 1 May 1048 by Bernold, Bishop of Utrecht.

spots.name: Traiectum
spots.summary: Traiectum was a Roman fort, on the frontier of the Roman Empire in Germania Inferior. The remains of the fort are in the center of Utrecht, Netherlands, which takes its name from the fort.

spots.name: Duitse Huis

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Duitse Huis is a complex of buildings in the city of Utrecht, Netherlands, protected as a national monument. The older parts date to a monastery of the Bailiwick of Utrecht of the Teutonic Knights founded in 1348. Originally Catholic, the order became Protestant during the Reformation.

spots.name: Vredenburg
spots.summary: Vredenburg Castle was a 16th-century castle built by Habsburg emperor Charles V in the city of Utrecht in the Netherlands. Some remains of the castle, which stood for only 50 years, are still visible on what is now Vredenburg square in Utrecht.

spots.name: TivoliVredenburg
spots.summary: The TivoliVredenburg is a contemporary music complex located in Utrecht, Netherlands. The venue consists of five halls designed acoustically for a specific music genre. Along with its halls, the venue also features an "amateur stage" and a cafe.

spots.name: Jacobikerk

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jacobikerk is a landmark Protestant church in Utrecht, Netherlands. The building is located on the St Jacobsstraat, named for its patron saint St. James the Greater. The church is one of the medieval parish churches of Utrecht, along with the Buurkerk, the Nikolaïkerk and the Geertekerk.

spots.name: Centraal Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Centraal Museum is the main museum in Utrecht, Netherlands, founded in 1838. The museum has a wide-ranging collection, mainly of works produced locally. The collection of the paintings by the Northern Mannerist Joachim Wtewael is by a long way the largest anywhere in the world.

spots.name: Railway Museum
spots.summary: The Railway Museum in Utrecht is the Dutch national railway museum. It was established in 1927 and since 1954 has been housed in the former Maliebaan station.

spots.name: Oudegracht
spots.summary: The Oudegracht, or "old canal", runs through the center of Utrecht, the Netherlands. It starts in the southeast of the city. Here the Kromme Rijn and the Vaartse Rijn arrive to meet the original moat of the fortified town, and the Oudegracht goes from there into the center of town.

spots.name: Museum Speelklok

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Museum Speelklok is a museum in Utrecht, Netherlands, specializing in self-playing musical instruments. Since 1984, it has been housed in the centre of Utrecht in a former church called Buurkerk.

spots.name: St. Willibrord's Church, Utrecht

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Willibrord's Church, Utrecht, is a Roman Catholic church operated by the traditionalist Society of Saint Pius X (SSPX) and dedicated to Saint Willibrord. It is at Minrebroederstraat 21, Utrecht, in the Netherlands and has been designated a rijksmonument since 1976.

spots.name: St. Gertrude's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Gertrude's Cathedral in Utrecht, the Netherlands, is the seat of the Archbishop of Utrecht and the mother church of the Old Catholic Church of the Netherlands.

spots.name: St. Mary's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Mary's Church, also called Mariakerk or Maria Maior, was one of five collegiate churches in the Dutch city of Utrecht, the others being St. Martin's Cathedral, St. Salvator's Church, the Pieterskerk, and the Janskerk.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Museum Catharijneconvent

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum Catharijneconvent is a museum of religious art in Utrecht, Netherlands. It is located in the former St. Catharine convent, having been sited there since 1979. Its collections include many artifacts from the museum of religious art of the Catholic Archbishopric of Utrecht, located in the convent until 1979.

spots.name: Winkel van Sinkel
spots.summary: De Winkel van Sinkel was the first department store in The Netherlands, built between 1837 and 1839 and located at Oudegracht 158 in Utrecht.

spots.name: Zuylen Castle

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Zuylen Castle is a Dutch castle at the village of Oud-Zuilen just north of the city of Utrecht. It is located along the river Vecht at the southern end of the Vechtstreek.

spots.name: Sonnenborgh Observatory

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sonnenborgh Observatory is an astronomical observatory and museum open to the public, located in Utrecht, Netherlands. It is located in one of the four stone forts built by Charles V as defense buildings for Utrecht.

spots.name: Muziekcentrum Vredenburg
spots.summary: Muziekcentrum Vredenburg was a music venue in Utrecht, Netherlands with a capacity of 5,000 people. It was designed by Dutch architect Herman Hertzberger. The venue hosted concerts by many famous artists, spanning many different genres.

spots.summary: The Sint-Salvator church was one of five Catholic Church collegiate churches in Utrecht, Netherlands, before the Protestant Reformation. The others were St. Martin's Cathedral, St. Peter's Church, St. John's church and St. Mary's church.

spots.name: Utrecht Post Office
spots.summary: The former Utrecht Main Post Office building completed in 1924, is situated on Neude square, Utrecht, the Netherlands. Since 2020 it has served as the headquarters of the Utrecht Public Library.

spots.name: St. Paul's Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Paul's Abbey was a monastery in Utrecht in the Netherlands. In 1580 it was the second oldest monastery in the Netherlands, second only to Egmond Abbey in the north.

spots.name: Dutch Water Defence Lines
spots.summary: The Dutch Water Defence lines is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Netherlands comprising the New Dutch Waterline and Stelling van Amsterdam. The Stelling van Amsterdam was added as a World Heritage Site in 1996, and was extended in 2021 with the New Dutch Waterline in 2021.

photo.author: Nanda Sluijsmans from Den Haag, Nederland

spots.name: Ulu Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ulu Mosque in Utrecht is located at the Mosque square; the first square or street in the Netherlands named after an Islamic religious building. Besides the Islamic prayer hall, the building also host a room for contemplation for people from any other denomination.

spots.name: The Letters of Utrecht
spots.summary: The Letters of Utrecht form an endless poem in the stones of a street in the center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. Every Saturday at 13:00, the next letter is hewn into the next cobblestone, with the intent to continue for as long as there are Saturdays. It takes about three years to publish an average sentence.

spots.name: St. Eloy's Hospice
spots.summary: St. Eloy's Hospice is a guildhall in Utrecht in the Netherlands.

spots.name: Moreelsebrug
spots.summary: The Moreelsebrug is a bicycle and pedestrian bridge in Utrecht, Netherlands, spanning the railroad tracks to the south of Utrecht Centraal railway station. It is about 275 metres long and connects the Dichterswijk with Mariaplaats in the Binnenstad district.

spots.summary: A notable building with a flying saucer (UFO) on its roof. The saucer is a remnant of the Utrecht art exhibition Panorama 2000, designed by Marc Ruygrok.

spots.name: Paushuize
spots.summary: Born in Utrecht, Adrianus VI, the sole Dutch pope and the last non-Italian pope until John Paul II, had this house constructed in 1517. It is used for congresses, weddings and group dinners.
